features.summary: Customers page: a server-paged list of storefront customers with tabs All, Active, Flagged, Suspended, Blocked (counts from one-row calls), search, a country filter, sorting, and a Data requests tab (customers:privacy). Customer page: header actions (edit, suspend or reactivate, block or unblock), five figures, and tabs Orders, Account (create an account, reset link or temporary password, sign out everywhere, last IP), Consents and data (consent evidence, the customer's data requests, export, anonymize), Risk and Support. The server owns every rule. The console shows problem+json refusals in the dialog that sent the call.

endpoints.query: Paging _start/_end, 25 per page (customers/lib/filters.ts:11). Filters: status (repeat = IN; tabs send one of active|suspended|blocked), riskLevel (repeat = IN; the Flagged tab sends riskLevel=medium&riskLevel=high, filters.ts:187), country (ISO-2, upper case), hasAccount=true|false. q: case-insensitive contains over name and email only (mocks/customerHandlers.ts:16; country is its own filter, M86). _sort is one of name|country|hasAccount|ordersCount|totalSpent|lastOrderAt|riskLevel|status, with _order asc|desc; default totalSpent desc (filters.ts:76-100). riskLevel sorts by order low<medium<high. Counts: five tab calls (no filter, status=active, riskLevel=medium&riskLevel=high, status=suspended, status=blocked) plus hasAccount=true, each _start=0&_end=1 with no toolbar filter (hooks/useCustomerCounts.ts:20-45). Palette: q=<text>&_start=0&_end=4 with no _sort, so the server's default order applies (lib/paletteSource.ts:10-21).
endpoints.response: JSON array + x-total-count. Row = customers columns: id, email, emailVerifiedAt, name, phone ('' when none), country, locale (en|ar), currency (currency id, see below), hasAccount, createdBy (staff id; null for self-signup or guest), marketingOptIn, riskLevel low|medium|high, status active|suspended|blocked|anonymized, suspendedAt, suspendedReason and suspendedBy (null unless suspended), internalNotes, lastLoginAt, firstOrderAt, totalSpent (4-dp USD, gross incl. VAT of non-rejected orders, '0.0000' when none), anonymizedAt, createdAt. Plus ordersCount (every order, any status), lastOrderAt (latest order created_at or null) and currencyCode (currencies.code); currency = currencies.id (JSON number) and currencyCode = currencies.code, both null when the customer has no currency: customers.currency stays the ISO code FK to currencies.code (as checkout_sessions and payments do) and every row builder (list, detail, create result, patch result) LEFT JOINs currencies ON currencies.code = customers.currency; request bodies carry no currency (create and a country change derive the code from the country and write the code). Never credential data. Anonymized rows carry name 'Deleted customer' and email deleted-<id>@redacted.invalid.

- account: null when hasAccount is false. Body {reason, note?}.

- note is optional, at most 200 chars, and left out when empty.

endpoints.request: No body. Moves suspended to active, clears suspended_at, suspended_reason and suspended_by, and writes audit_logs (scenario b2c-account step 9).

Body {blocked: true, reason} or {blocked: false}.
- reason is one of 'Chargeback or dispute', 'Card testing or fraud', 'Abuse of refunds', 'Other' (lib/status.ts:55-60).
- {blocked: false} carries no reason; accept an optional one.
Block: sets status blocked and risk_level high. Adds to blocklist_entries, each with source manual, the reason, created_by = caller and customer_id = the customer: kind email (the normalised email hash), kind card for each distinct non-null payments.card_fingerprint of the customer's payments, kind imei for each distinct IMEI on the customer's orders and checkout sessions still stored (device = IMEI per M106/B77; kind 'device' stays non-addable). Inserts use ON CONFLICT (kind, value_hash) DO NOTHING: an existing entry (from a risk refund, chargeback, manual add or another customer's block) is kept unchanged and not linked. Only this route sets blocklist_entries.customer_id; the risk refund route and manual adds leave it null. Revokes sessions.
Unblock: sets status active, moves risk_level high to medium, and deletes only the entries WHERE customer_id = :id AND source = 'manual'.
Writes audit_logs both ways. Card fingerprint = the gateway's card fingerprint (for example Stripe payment_method.card.fingerprint, never card data), written by the B2C payment webhook into the new payments.card_fingerprint column (partial index where not null).

No CSRF token is sent on this GET (apiDownload sends none). Content-Disposition is already in CORS_EXPOSED_HEADERS.

The console falls back to that name when the header is missing; expose the header through CORS. Works for every customer, anonymized ones included.

businessRules:
Status machine:
- active to suspended (suspend, reason required); suspended to active (reactivate).
- active or suspended to blocked (block, reason required); blocked to active (unblock).
- any status to anonymized (irreversible).
Other moves answer 409 (NOT_ACTIVE, NOT_SUSPENDED, ALREADY_BLOCKED, NOT_BLOCKED). Every action and PATCH on an anonymized customer answers 409 ANONYMIZED (mocks/actionHandlers.ts:31-38, 45-46, 135-179; customerHandlers.ts:116-118).

Suspend ends all sessions and refuses sign-in and new checkout sessions with ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED; paid orders in progress still complete, and nothing goes to the blocklist (map POST /admin/customers/:id/suspend; scenario b2c-account steps 7-8).

Block is for fraud. It adds the email hash, plus card fingerprints and devices, to blocklist_entries (source manual, with the reason) and raises risk_level to high. Unblock lowers high to medium and lifts those entries (demo 12-state-b2c.js:47-53; mocks/actionHandlers.ts:162-179).

Email is unique across all customers, guests included, compared case-insensitively, on create and edit: 409 EMAIL_TAKEN. A blocklisted email is refused on create and on an email change (scenario b2c-account step 1; demo 12-state-b2c.js:79-80, 104-106). Anonymize rewrites the email, so the old address is free again unless it is blocklisted.

Passwords are never readable or logged.
- Temporary passwords: generated by the server (14 chars from the demo alphabet without look-alike characters), stored as a hash with must_change_password, and returned once as temporaryPassword.
- Invite and reset links: single-use auth_tokens valid one hour, hash only.
(Map POST /admin/customers/:id/password; auth_tokens description; mocks/context.ts:27-30; M85.)
Changing an account's email clears email_verified_at (map customers row description; customerHandlers.ts:134-135). Changing the country re-derives the currency (customerHandlers.ts:138-147).

Anonymize keeps payment records. It replaces name, email, phone and notes; drops the marketing opt-in, credentials and sessions; and cuts stored IMEIs to the TAC on orders, checkout sessions and IMEI checks. Ticket requester and author names then read 'Deleted customer' (map POST /admin/customers/:id/anonymize; demo 12-state-b2c.js:152-162; mocks/actionHandlers.ts:182-201).

Export closes the customer's open or in_progress export request, and anonymize closes their erasure request. Both set completed with completed_at and handled_by, in the same transaction as the audit entry (M74; mocks/actionHandlers.ts:49-64, 96, 200).

Data requests are created by POST /store/v1/me/data-export (kind export) and /store/v1/me/data-delete (kind erasure), with due_at = requested_at + 30 days (demo S.dsr). Moves: open to in_progress, completed or rejected; in_progress to completed or rejected. A closed request answers 409 REQUEST_CLOSED (mocks/requestHandlers.ts:13, 46-55; components/DataRequestTable.tsx:117-134).

Figures:
- totalSpent = sum of (total_price + tax_amount) in USD over the customer's orders whose status is not rejected.
- ordersCount counts every order.
- firstOrderAt and lastOrderAt come from orders.created_at.
Keep customers.total_spent and first_order_at in step with order status changes (demo custStats 12-state-b2c.js:20-31; mocks/dto.ts:19-32).

Permissions (M7, route manifest):
- list and show: customers:read; create: customers:create; PATCH and account: customers:update.
- password and sessions/revoke: customers:password.
- suspend and reactivate: customers:suspend; block: customers:block.
- export, anonymize and data-requests: customers:privacy.
Every action writes audit_logs with before and after, never a password.

features.summary:
Storefront page with five tabs:
- Services on sale: listings per service and language, the On the site switch, a retail-price dialog checked against the server's floor, and counts.
- Landing pages: kind filter, publish and unpublish, and the draft generator.
- Content and legal: static and blog pages loaded whole; legal versions are written as drafts, then published.
- Help centre: article CRUD, with the publish switch done through PATCH.
- TAC catalogue: CRUD without delete.
Figures are one-row count calls. Every price, floor, margin and lock comes from the server. PATCH /admin/storefront/settings belongs to the settings feature.

businessRules: The Retail price is service_group_prices.price for the single b2c_retail group: net USD before VAT, one per service, for all locales. Storefront checkouts price from it, add the country's VAT, and lock the result on the session (scenario b2c-paid step 3; service_group_prices description; M182; components/PriceDialog.tsx:52-57).

Selling below the floor is blocked: refuse retailPrice <= 0 and retailPrice < floorPrice, with 422 on retailPrice. floorPrice = basePrice x 1.10 (demo retailFloor, 12-state-b2c.js:355), and never below the service's own floor, cost + minProfit (map service-listings description; listingRoutes.ts:106-126).

A locked listing cannot be switched on, priced or created: 409 LISTING_LOCKED. Locked means the service is never public: its category is hidden from the b2c_retail group, or the service is disabled. Switching on a listing whose service is disabled answers 409 SERVICE_DISABLED (demo setListed 12-state-b2c.js:356-364; listingRoutes.ts:64-71, 110-141).

Slugs are made from the title when empty, with the demo's slugOf. They are unique per locale for pages and listings (409 SLUG_TAKEN or LISTING_EXISTS, with errors[].field). Each service has one listing per locale (mocks/http.ts:69-76; pageRoutes.ts:30-39; listingRoutes.ts:72-83).

Content pages:
- Created as drafts.
- Status changes only through POST /:id/publish: published true sets published with published_at; false sets draft.
- PATCH never changes kind or status.
- The generator only creates drafts and skips slugs that exist.
(Map content-pages rows; pageRoutes.ts:41-59, 63-117.)

Legal versions are immutable (there is no edit route).
- POST creates a draft: is_current false, effective_from null.
- Publish, in one transaction, retires the current version of the same type and locale (is_current false, effective_from kept) and makes this one current from now. Later consents reference it.
- An already current version answers 409 ALREADY_CURRENT; a duplicate version per type and locale answers 409 VERSION_EXISTS.
(Map legal rows; legalRoutes.ts:24-45, 72-78; lib/legal.ts:66-74.)

TAC: exactly 8 digits and unique (409 TAC_TAKEN on tac). brand and model are required; marketingName and releaseYear are optional. Console entries get source manual. No delete (map CRUD[LSCU]; tacRoutes.ts:35-84).
Help articles have no publish route: the switch is PATCH {isPublished} under storefront:update. New articles are unpublished by default and go last in sort order (helpRoutes.ts:39-50; M187).

Permissions (M7, M187):
- storefront:* rows: storefront:read, storefront:create, storefront:update; page publish: storefront:publish; generator: storefront:create.
- legal:* rows: legal:read, legal:create; legal publish: legal:publish.
- TAC: catalog:read, catalog:create, catalog:update.
Publishes write audit_logs (map tables).
Languages are en and ar only (mocks/http.ts:79); other locales answer 422 on locale.

features.summary: Abandoned checkouts page: a server-paged list (12 per page) of people who left an email at checkout. Each row carries the server's marketing-consent and canRecover verdicts. The page has a 'Needs a reminder' filter (canRecover=true), search on the full email, and Remind (one row or the ticked rows) through POST /admin/checkouts/recover, whose answer reports the sent and skipped checkouts. A Sales funnel panel (reports:growth) shows four counts for 7, 30 or 90 days. The consent rule is the server's (M1).

features.summary:
Support page:
- Inbox: Open, Overdue, Mine, Resolved and All filters, a Who filter and search; 25 per page, late tickets first, refreshed every 30 s; figures from one-row count calls.
- Thread pane: read by id, messages embedded (internal notes included), with priority, assignee, Resolve and Reopen controls.
- Composer: replies by email or Telegram, internal notes, templates filled in the browser.
- Templates view: reply-templates CRUD.
The customer page embeds a customer's latest tickets. The timers (late, slaDueAt, lastPublicAt) are the server's.

endpoints.query:
Paging 25. Filters:
- status: repeat = IN. Open sends new&open&pending; Resolved sends resolved. status=pending is translated to the stored pending_customer (status IN (pending_customer)) by the status codec.
- late=true: Overdue.
- assigneeId=<me>: Mine.
- requesterType=customer|client: Who.
- requesterId=<customer id> with requesterType=customer: link from a customer.
- q: contains over number, subject and requester name.
Sort: _sort=late,updatedAt&_order=desc,desc; the Resolved filter sends updatedAt desc only (lib/filters.ts:152-175).
Counts, each with _start=0&_end=1, every 30 s: status=new&status=open&status=pending; status=new; late=true; status=resolved (hooks/useTicketCounts.ts:18-34).
Customer page: requesterType=customer&requesterId=<id>&_sort=updatedAt&_order=desc&_start=0&_end=10 (hooks/useCustomerTickets.ts:8-16).
Palette: q&_start=0&_end=3&_sort=updatedAt&_order=desc.
The list itself is also refetched every 30 s.
endpoints.response:
JSON array + x-total-count. Row:
- id, number (server-made, 'T-1042' style), subject.
- channel email|web|chat|telegram.
- requesterType customer|client, requesterId, requester {name, email or null}.
- orderId or null, category (one of 8 words), priority high|normal|low.
- status: only new|open|pending|resolved (the stored pending_customer is sent as pending: status codec, B112; closed is removed from the stored vocabulary so it can never reach the console). Any other word crashes the badge (TicketStatusBadge.tsx:7-8).
- assigneeId or null, and assignee {id, name} or null.
- slaDueAt: when the next reply is due; null when nobody is waiting.
- firstResponseAt, resolvedAt.
- csatScore: 1-5 or null.
- createdAt, updatedAt (last activity).
- lastPublicAt: time of the latest non-internal message, or null.
- late: a reply is awaited and slaDueAt has passed; always false when resolved.
endpoints.mapConflict: Rows need joins to customers or clients (requester), staff_users (assignee) and ticket_messages (lastPublicAt); the route's tables are support_tickets and orders. The map computes sla_due_at by category at creation (b2c-ticket step 2), while the demo uses priority targets of 2h, 8h and 24h. Proposal: the category sets the default priority; sla_due_at = time of the last customer message + the priority's target, recomputed when the customer writes or the priority changes, and null after a public staff reply.

endpoints.request: :id is the numeric ticket id. The pane reads it by id, whatever the list shows.
endpoints.response:
The list row plus:
- messages[], oldest first, internal notes included. Each has id, ticketId, authorType customer|client|staff|system, authorId or null, authorName (joined; 'Deleted customer' after anonymize; 'System' for system messages), body, isInternal, fileIds (number[]) and createdAt.
- replyChannels: ['email'], plus 'telegram' when the requester has a linked Telegram chat.
Refetched every 30 s while open.
endpoints.mapConflict: The map has no messages route, so the thread rides on this answer and needs ticket_messages, which is not in the route's tables.

endpoints.request:
Partial body {priority?, assigneeId?, status?}. Status codec (B112): the body word pending is stored as pending_customer; status accepts only new|open|pending|resolved (anything else is 422 on status); stored words other than pending_customer pass through. Status codec in one place, the support repository: toWire(pending_customer) = 'pending', fromWire('pending') = 'pending_customer'.
- assigneeId: null unassigns; otherwise it must be an active staff member.
- status 'resolved': sets resolved_at now, adds an internal system message 'Marked resolved by <name>. A satisfaction survey is emailed to the customer.', and sends the CSAT survey (outbox/notifications).
- status 'open' (reopen): only from resolved; sets resolved_at null.
Values equal to the current ones are ignored. audit_logs entry per change.
endpoints.response: 200 with the updated list row (no messages).
endpoints.mapConflict: The route's tables are support_tickets and orders, but resolving also writes ticket_messages, notifications/outbox_events and audit_logs (b2c-ticket steps 7-8).

Body {body, channel?}.
- body: trimmed text; templates are already filled in by the console.
- channel: email|telegram, sent only when replyChannels has more than one entry (Composer.tsx:48-51, 91). Without it, use the ticket's channel when allowed, else email.
Effects: inserts a staff message (is_internal false) and delivers it on the channel. The first public reply sets first_response_at. A new or open ticket becomes pending_customer (sent as pending, see the status codec), and sla_due_at becomes null. An unassigned ticket is assigned to the sender. updated_at is set.
endpoints.response: 201 with the new TicketMessage.

the ticket is resolved; reopen it first (mocks/ticketHandlers.ts:79-81)

When the total exceeds 200, the view says so. businessRules:
SLA: priority targets are high 2h, normal 8h, low 24h (demo PRIO_TARGET).
- sla_due_at = time of the latest customer-side public message + the target. It is set at creation and whenever the customer writes, and recomputed on a priority change.
- It becomes null after a public staff reply or on resolve.
- late = sla_due_at < now AND status <> resolved.
The late=true filter and the sort on late run in SQL (mocks/dto.ts:8-35; M143, M144).

Reply on a resolved ticket answers 409 TICKET_RESOLVED. The first public reply sets first_response_at. An unassigned ticket is assigned to whoever replies, and also to whoever writes a note. updated_at becomes the message time (mocks/ticketHandlers.ts:42-54, 79-81; scenario b2c-ticket step 4).

Internal notes (is_internal) never reach the customer: they are left out of store ticket reads and emails, and included in GET /admin/support-tickets/:id (map note row; GET /store/v1/tickets/:token without internal notes).

Resolve writes resolved_at and an internal system message 'Marked resolved by <staff>. A satisfaction survey is emailed to the customer.', sends the CSAT survey (notification) and writes an audit entry. Reopen clears resolved_at (mocks/ticketHandlers.ts:146-166; demo ticketSet 12-state-b2c.js:200-208; scenario b2c-ticket steps 7-8).

Reply channels: email always (the requester's email); telegram only when the requester has a linked Telegram chat. A channel outside replyChannels answers 422 on channel. Without a channel, the reply uses the ticket's channel when allowed, else email (M148; Composer.tsx:48-51, 91; mocks/ticketHandlers.ts:72-76).

Templates: title, body, category (the ticket category words) and locale (en|ar) are required. shortcut is optional: '' or starting with '/', and unique when non-empty (409 SHORTCUT_TAKEN). The body is stored raw with {{name}}, {{order}} and {{eta}}. The console fills the variables, and the server stores the reply text as sent (mocks/templateHandlers.ts:15-42; M142, M151).
The assignee must be an active staff member (422 on assigneeId); null unassigns (mocks/ticketHandlers.ts:127-131; TicketControls.tsx:44).

Permissions (M7):
- read: support:read.
- PATCH (priority, assignee, status): support:update.
- reply and note: support:reply.
- templates: support:create, support:update, support:delete.
The assignee menu reads GET /admin/staff only with staff:read (useAssignees.ts:11). Changes write audit_logs.
